newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica trucking strike to start Wednesday - union.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica trucking strike to start Wednesday - union.

text.p: Union and employer representatives in the trucking industry failed to resolve a wage deadlock late on Monday, paving the way for a national strike by around 50,000 workers on Wednesday, a union official said.
Transport and General Workers' Union (TGWU) national organiser Thulani Dlamini told Reuters on Tuesday talks on Monday night to avert the strike had failed.
"As the situation stands at the moment the strike will go ahead on Wednesday morning," Dlamini said.
He said the union had put forward a non-negotiable "showstopper" on Monday, revising its original wage demand of between 14 and 18 percent across-the-board to 12.5 percent.
However, employers had not agreed to the final demand and the seven unions organised in the industry were ready to go on strike early on Wednesday.
Employers, represented by the the Road Freight Association, last week raised their offer from nine percent across-the-board to ten percent.
Dlamini said employers would be meeting on Tuesday to discuss the wage deadlock and had undertaken to report back to the union on the outcome of their discussions by Tuesday afternoon.
The strike could affect major sectors in the economy such as banking, air freight, waste companies, livestock vehicles, and the ferrying of chemicals and fuels.
Trucker blockades on major highways are also a possibility if employers do not confiscate trucks.

Seven unions are organised in the industry, including the TGWU, the Professional Transport Workers' Union, African Miners and Allied Workers, the Turning Wheel Workers' Union, the Motor Transport Workers' Union, the South African Transport Workers' Union and the Transport and Allied Workers' Union.
The average wage in the industry is 321 rand per week for general workers in the bigger centres.
